textRuns.value: Left: summer heat and rainfall at the two weather stations either side of Bristol, every year on record; 2026 was the hottest summer at both. Right: how Bristol's council trees responded each summer since 2018, measured from satellite images; below zero means less chlorophyll than in a tree's own normal years. Although the weather was extreme, the trees held up about as well as in the 2018 drought: more trees were affected in 2026, but not more deeply.
